Package ui11

Class Widget

java.lang.Object
ui11.Widget
All Implemented Interfaces:
Cloneable
Direct Known Subclasses:
Provider, SubstitutedWidget
public abstract class Widget extends Object implements Cloneable
This class represents the basic building block for user interface components. A widget can be for example a simple geometric shape, a layout which arranges other widgets, a control, or a region an application.

A widget describes part of the user interface by building a constellation of other widgets that describe the user interface more concretely. The building process continues recursively until the description of the user interface is fully concrete (TODO ezt definiálni kéne).

Every non-static fields of the subtypes of this subclass must be either final or annotated with @Inject or @Remember.

  • Method Details

    • initState

      protected void initState()
      Called when the widget is added to the tree and no previous state is available.

      After calling this method, onResume() then build() will be called. Then build() will be called again and again whenever an input property or an observable value changes.

      Note: Don't pass a reference to this value to other objects which last longer than this Widget instance, because while the same conceptual widget appears on the screen and shares the same state, the actual instances may be recreated whoever instantiates this widget.

    • onResume

      protected void onResume()
      Called when the widget is added to the tree.

      Before calling this method, initState() is called if no previous state is available. After calling this method then build() will be called. Then build() will be called again and again whenever an input property or a subscribed observable value changes.

      Note: Don't pass a reference to this value to other objects which last longer than this Widget instance, because while the same conceptual widget appears on the screen and shares the same state, the actual instances may be recreated whoever instantiates this widget.$

    • build

      protected abstract Widget build()
      Builds the content of the widget.

      The framework calls method annotated with this annotation when this widget is inserted into the tree newly, or if its input values was changed, or the observable dependencies of this widget change. This method can potentially be called in every frame and should not have any side effects beyond building a widget.

      This method must not return null.

    • untilNextRebuild

      protected final ui11.observable.Scope untilNextRebuild() throws IllegalStateException
      Returns a Scope that will be open until the next build() rebuild.

      This method can be only called from build().

      At the moment when this scope is closed, the inherited value observables obtained via @Inject will be the same in the last build.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called not in build()

    • untilPause

      protected final ui11.observable.Scope untilPause() throws IllegalStateException
      Returns a Scope that will be open until this widget is removed from the widget tree.

      This method can be only called after the widget is added to the tree and initState() has been finished.

      At the moment when this scope is closed, the inherited value observables obtained via @Inject can still be seen, but their values might be obsolete.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called when this widget is not in the widget tree, or build() hasn't ran yet

    • listenerProxy

      protected final Runnable listenerProxy(Runnable listener)
      The specified object will be replaced by a proxy object, which implements the interface, and forwards all method calls to the element's current widget's value of the annotated field. This allows to change event listener implementations without rebuilding the widgets.

      If the listener argument is null, then it won't be replaced by a proxy object.

    • withID

      protected final @NonNull Widget withID(@NonNull String id, @NonNull Widget content)
      Assigns an ID to a widget. A new widget will only be used to update an existing widget state if its ID is the same as the IDs of the current widget; otherwise, a new widget state will be created.

      IDs are not global: their scope is only this widget from which you call this method. If you call this method from another widget with the same ID argument, the IDs won't collide.

    • equals

      public boolean equals(Object obj)
      Compares the input fields of the other widget. Input field means a final non-static field of a Widget subtype, which is not annotated with Widget.Inject or Widget.Remember. This also includes non-static final fields annotated with containing a listener proxy.

      Note that this method is not used for determining that a widget needs rebuild. Instead, for determining that a widget needs rebuild or not a slightly different approach used which differs only in the treatment of listener proxy fields: they are not compared by value (or the delegate of the proxy object in them), but only the nullness is compared to the same field of the other object.

      Overrides:
      equals in class Object
      Returns:
      true of the specified object is the same class as this object and the values of all non-listener input fields are equal (according to Objects.equals) to the same fields of this object
